articleHeadline: Hantavirus: What we know about the Atlantic cruise ship outbreak
articleSummary: Three people have died after a suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean, en route from Argentina to Cape Verde. One case is confirmed and five are under investigation, with ongoing laboratory testing. Hantavirus is rodent-borne, mainly transmitted by inhaling dried rodent droppings; bites are rare. It can cause HPS—fatigue, fever, muscle aches, headaches, abdominal symptoms—with mortality around 38% if respiratory symptoms develop. HFRS mainly affects kidneys, causing low blood pressure and kidney failure. Global HFRS cases total about 150,000 annually, mainly in Europe and Asia; more than half occur in China. articleSummary: Stimulated plasma IP-10 shows high diagnostic performance for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) among healthcare workers in a high TB-burden setting in Thailand. articleSummary: Three deaths followed a suspected hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius in the Atlantic Ocean. One laboratory-confirmed case was reported, with five others under investigation, and detailed testing is underway, per the WHO. The vessel was traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde when the event was identified. Hantavirus is a rodent-borne group transmitted mainly by inhaling aerosolized urine, droppings, or saliva; transmission by bites is rare. It can cause two severe diseases: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). Globally, about 150,000 HFRS cases occur annually, mainly in Europe and Asia, with more than half in China. In the US (1993–2023) there have been 890 cases; Seoul virus is widespread. No specific treatment exists; management is supportive, including oxygen, respiratory support, antivirals, and dialysis for severe cases. A February 2025 US death (Betsy Arakawa) was linked to hantavirus (HPS).

articleSummary: Taiwan's main circulating hantavirus is Seoul virus. Most infections are asymptomatic or mild; about 1–10% of infected individuals seek medical care; overall mortality remains low. Taiwan CDC data show hantavirus syndrome had zero domestic cases from 2016–2020; since 2021 only sporadic locally acquired cases. For 2022–2025, annual confirmed cases were 2, 4, 3, and 3, respectively; by May 2026, 2 cases were recorded. There has been a single hantavirus-related death in the past 25 years, this year, 2026. Seoul virus, prevalent in Taiwan, is similar to strains in Korea and Japan and tends to cause milder disease, whereas China’s hantaan virus can be more severe. A separate international report of an Atlantic cruise hantavirus cluster suggested American-type hantavirus causing hantavirus pulmonary syndrome with higher fatality, but the virus type is unconfirmed. High-risk individuals should avoid high-risk environments if possible.

articleSummary: India faces a summer fever outbreak affecting a large portion of the population. Symptoms include altered mental state, nausea, vomiting, rapid breathing, rapid heart rate, and throbbing headache. articleHeadline: What is hantavirus and how deadly is it?
articleSummary: On 2026-05-04, hantavirus caused a deadly outbreak aboard the MV Hondius, a cruise ship of Oceanwide Expeditions traveling in the southern Atlantic from Argentina to Cape Verde. Hantaviruses circulate in rodents and can cause respiratory and cardiac distress and hemorrhagic fevers; there are no vaccines or specific antivirals, with treatment limited to symptom relief. Transmission occurs via infected rodents' saliva, urine, or droppings, or inhalation of contaminated dust; human-to-human spread is extremely rare. Diagnosis can be confirmed by hantavirus-specific IgM antibodies. The two main syndromes are hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, which can cause pulmonary edema and acute respiratory failure, and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe/Asia. Incubation: HPS 1–8 weeks; HFRS 1–2 weeks to eight weeks. Global case counts: ~200 HPS/year (Americas; CFR ~40%), 150,000–200,000 HFRS/year (worldwide; CFR 1–12%, China). WHO notes the risk to the public is low; no panic or travel restrictions.

articleHeadline: Serendipitous detection of invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi in Kisumu, Kenya in June 2022 - Scientific Reports
articleSummary: Anopheles stephensi, an invasive malaria vector spreading across Africa since its first identification in Djibouti in 2012, was serendipitously detected in Kisumu City, western Kenya, during mid-2022 bloodmeal analyses at an urban slaughterhouse. In a pool of five morphologically classified An. gambiae s.l., one pool yielded ASVs with BLAST matches to An. stephensi (19.6% of ASVs). This marks the first report of An. stephensi south of the Equator. As of 2025, An. stephensi has been identified in eight other countries (Ethiopia, Sudan, Somaliland, Eritrea, Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Niger). The finding underscores need for continued entomological and malaria case surveillance to assess shifting vector dynamics and vector-livestock interactions, informing future control strategies.

articleSummary: Hantavirus comprises rodent-borne viruses; transmission occurs mainly by inhalation of particles from the urine, saliva, or feces of infected rodents. Worldwide, about 150,000 cases are estimated annually, with higher incidence in Asia, especially China, and rising levels in Europe. Two clinical forms exist: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, with mortality up to 38%, and Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) in Europe and Asia, causing kidney injury and potential acute renal failure. The MV Hondius cruise outbreak off Cape Verde, en route between Argentina and Cape Verde, has three deaths and three critically ill; infections are believed to have occurred before boarding, with incubation ranging from two weeks to two months. Early symptoms resemble influenza; progression yields respiratory failure in HPS or shock and renal failure in HFRS. No specific antiviral exists; management is supportive, including oxygen and ventilation. Human transmission is rare except for Andes virus cases.

articleHeadline: Geometric deep learning enables high-fidelity network imputation for HIV transmission modeling - Communications Medicine
articleSummary: HIV transmission modeling among people who inject drugs (PWID) in New Delhi, India, benefits from geometric deep learning. A graph neural network (GNN) predicted injection partnerships in a longitudinal study of 2,512 PWID using demographic, behavioral, and spatial-venue data, outperforming exponential random graph models (ERGMs). The imputed network showed strong structural concordance to the empirical network (spectral similarity 0.87), and venue data increased accuracy from 51.0% to 60.8% (precision 59.4%, recall 67.9%, F1 63.4%). In an external cohort, the GNN retained performance (F1 61.3%), capturing structural changes. When calibrating a HIV transmission model on the GNN-imputed versus empirical network, incidence curves differed by at most 0.4 infections per 100 person-years over two years after venue-scale interventions. Demonstrates that GNN-based imputation preserves epidemiologically relevant network structure and HIV intervention conclusions when full sociometric data are infeasible.

articleSummary: Argentina’s Ministry of Health reports ongoing hantavirus monitoring on the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius, currently anchored off Cape Verde. Passengers and crew are isolated, with symptomatic individuals receiving care. articleSummary: One confirmed hantavirus case and five suspected aboard the polar cruise MV Hondius, triggering a global alert as the WHO coordinates investigations. The ship (107.6 m, Oceanwide Expeditions) departed Ushuaia, Argentina, with 170 passengers and 70 crew. Reports indicate three fatalities on board. Transmission is mainly via inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta; exposure to urine, feces, or saliva can also spread the virus, with bites occasionally possible. Hantavirus can cause two severe diseases: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), which starts with fatigue, fever, and myalgias and can progress to fatal respiratory failure (mortality ~38% when respiratory symptoms develop); and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), which damages kidneys and may cause hypotension and acute kidney failure. Globally, 150,000–200,000 HFRS cases are reported annually; China accounts for over half. The Seoul hantavirus lineage has been detected worldwide, including the United States (890 cases 1993–2023). Laboratory confirmation is ongoing as of May 4, 2026.

articleSummary: Brazil’s Anvisa authorized Instituto Butantan to manufacture the chikungunya vaccine, Butantan-Chik, enabling its inclusion in the SUS for adults 18–59 years exposed to the virus. Butantan will be the official production site in Brazil; previously production was registered at Valneva’s factories in France and Austria. Regulators approved the vaccine in April 2025. Butantan director Esper Kallás said the public institution can deliver the vaccine at lower cost with the same safety and efficacy. Clinical data from U.S. trials (≥4,000 volunteers aged 18–65) showed 98.9% developed neutralizing antibodies, with a tolerable safety profile and mild-to-moderate adverse events (headache, myalgia, fatigue, fever). In February 2026, Butantan-Chik began rollout in SUS in high-incidence municipalities under a Health Ministry pilot. Beyond Brazil, the vaccine also has approvals in Canada, Europe, and the United Kingdom.

articleHeadline: 'HFMD cases rising in Kashmir, keep infected children home'
articleSummary: HFMD cases rising in Kashmir's Valley hospitals; Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease is highly contagious but typically mild, mainly affecting children under five. Caused by enteroviruses, chiefly Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71, it spreads via saliva, droplets, and blister fluid, thriving in schools and daycare. Early symptoms include low-to-moderate fever, sore throat, reduced appetite, irritability, followed by mouth ulcers after 1–2 days and a non-itchy rash on hands and feet (sometimes buttocks, knees, elbows). Most cases are self-limiting; no antiviral exists. Management is supportive: fever control, adequate hydration, and pain relief. Return to school after 5–7 days; keep infected children home for about a week with strict hand hygiene and avoidance of kissing/hugging. Warning signs warranting medical attention include dehydration, fever persisting >3 days, lethargy, vomiting, or breathing difficulties.

articleHeadline: Burundi: Cholera outbreak DREF Operational Update - MDRBI024 - Burundi
articleSummary: Cholera re-emerged in Burundi in early 2025, driven by unsafe water from Lake Tanganyika, poor hygiene and sanitation, and inadequate latrines in schools. Initial foci were Cibitoke, Bubanza, Bujumbura, and Rumonge, but transmission surged in Lake Nyanza health district, with daily cases often over 50. The first case was reported November 27, 2025, in Sangtaire (Lac Nyanza). Between Nov 27 and Dec 7, 2025, cumulative cases rose from 2,689 to 2,968 (279 new cases in one week). The epicenter remained Nyanza Lac, and flooding during the 2025-2026 season worsened water and sanitation, raising cross-border spread risk from DRC. By April 12–13, 2026, the Nyanza Lac outbreak was brought under control, but cases increased again in Bujumbura Municipality's Mukaza, Kamenge, and Mutimbuzi. MoH reported 806 cumulative cases with 37 active cases (as of Apr 13, 2026).

articleHeadlineTranslated: What do we know about hantavirus?
articleHeadline: درباره هانتاویروس چه می‌دانیم؟
articleSummary: Three deaths attributed to hantavirus on the MV Hondius cruise in the central Atlantic Ocean, en route to Cape Verde, with one laboratory-confirmed case and five suspected cases under investigation, per WHO. Hantaviruses are rodent-borne and predominantly spread to humans through inhalation of aerosolized urine, droppings, or saliva from infected rodents; bites or scratches are rare transmission routes. Two severe diseases can occur: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) begins with fatigue, fever, and myalgias, then may cause respiratory distress; CDC notes ~38% mortality with respiratory involvement. The second, Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), mainly affects the kidneys and can cause hypotension, internal bleeding, and acute kidney failure. Global estimates suggest about 150,000 HFRS cases annually, mainly in Europe and Asia, with notable activity in China. In the US, surveillance from 1993–2023 records 890 cases. Seoul virus is a major lineage found worldwide, including the United States. No specific antivirals exist; care is supportive (oxygen, ventilation, dialysis). Prevention focuses on reducing rodent exposure and sealing entry points; use protection when cleaning rodent droppings.
notes: 記事サマリーはハンタウイルス全般の疾病背景情報を提供している。具体的なアウトブレイクイベント（MV Hondius船での死亡例）は大西洋中央での国際航行中の船舶が主舞台であり、対象国リスト内での実発生地は特定不可。ただし記事でChinaについてHFRSの世界的流行地として明示的に言及されている（「notable activity in China」）ため、Chinaのみ verified_locations に含める。集団発生の詳細情報（患者数内訳、感染ルート特定等）が限定的であるが、船舶環境での集団ケースは管理・防疫上の公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。
